minutes.headline: Commission approved a septic replacement, a Keolis rail-line spray plan, a well, and tree removal for a new house — but rejected an over-the-wetland deck walkway as built
minutes.summary: This was a routine Conservation Commission hearing night: several small wetlands permits (septic replacement, well drilling, a rail right-of-way herbicide plan, tree removal near a new house build) were approved with conditions, and several other hearings were continued to future dates. The commission firmly declined to retroactively permit a homeowner's patio/walkway/stairs built inside the 30-foot no-disturb buffer at 67 Island Road, telling the applicant to work with an engineer and come back; it also turned away an application to clear shoreline trees for solar panels at 10 Sandy Cove as outside what current bylaws allow. The board created an associate-commissioner slot (to be filled after outgoing member Mary Wilson's term ends), approved a small purchase for the pollinator habitat, and discussed process issues (a new interim conservation agent, default-continuation practice, notice timelines).

decisions.decision: For 60 Cross Road, the commission informally agreed the revised house plan likely qualifies as a modified order of conditions rather than requiring a brand-new notice of intent, pending formal discussion at the next meeting since it could not be legally opened tonight.

On a straw poll, the commission indicated it would not permit tree removal for solar panels at 10 Sandy Cove under current bylaws and suggested the applicant reconsider or wait for regulation changes.
Advised the resident at 42 Meadow Lane to file a formal RDA (rather than proceed informally or as an administrative determination) for landscaping/fill work near the buffer.
Agreed to track a new debris issue at 40 Fire Road/12 as a separate enforcement matter and to file for a certificate of compliance once the town places boulders as the final condition.
Agreed to hold off appointing Mary Wilson to the new associate-commissioner position until she is no longer a sitting commissioner, likely at the July meeting.
Agreed offline follow-up is still needed to scope numbers for an RFQ for third-party (horizontal) engineering peer review.
Agreed to seek a short meeting with the town's outside counsel (Adam Costa) to confirm the commission's understanding of its default-continuation practice for absent/incomplete applicants.
Agreed to ask the incoming interim conservation agent how the neighboring town (Fitchburg), which meets only monthly, complies with the 21-day notice-to-act requirement.

what_happened.line: Commission declined to retroactively permit a deck, walkway and stairs built inside the wetland no-disturb buffer at 67 Island Road, continuing the case to June 18 and directing an engineer-led redesign.
Approved, with conditions, a failed septic replacement on Northfield Road, a well and water line on Round Road, a rail right-of-way herbicide plan, and tree removal tied to a new house build.
Indicated by straw poll it would not permit shoreline tree removal for solar panels at 10 Sandy Cove under the current bylaw.
Voted to create a new associate-commissioner seat, to be filled after outgoing member Mary Wilson's term ends.
Approved a purchase for the pollinator habitat, plants and a string trimmer, paid from the habitat fund.

why_it_matters: Property owners near wetlands: the buffer rule was enforced against work already built, not waived after the fact, which sets the standard for anyone doing landscaping near a wetland or shoreline.
Anyone proposing shoreline tree clearing, including for solar, learned the current bylaw does not allow it without a regulation change.
Septic, well and rail-corridor permits were approved with conditions, the routine path most wetlands-area projects in town follow.
